name: return28-foreign-fcy
description: Form 1116 with FOREIGN-CURRENCY intake (the 15CA/15CB path): the Indian property-sale gain and TDS arrive in rupees plus one user-chosen exchange rate; the KERNEL converts with the arithmetic on the record AND reports the converted gain itself — no separate US-side capital-gain entry exists in the facts (P25). The converted gain enters via Schedule D (all long-term here), so it lands in total income, the preferential-rate stack, AGI, and IL automatically. 4,175,000 INR gain and 835,000 INR TDS at 83.5 INR/USD convert to exactly the 50,000 / 10,000 USD of return27 — every downstream line must match return27 to the dollar.
note: HAND-VERIFIED: 4,175,000 ÷ 83.5 = 50,000.00 → 50,000; 835,000 ÷ 83.5 = 10,000.00 → 10,000. Sch D: LT 50,000, ST 0 → line 16 = 50,000, net capital gain 50,000 (all preferential). From there identical to return27 (see its note): total income 150,000, taxable 135,000, tax 22,000, §904 limitation 3,303, credit 3,303, unused 6,697, owe 3,697. CONTRAST with return27: there the foreign concepts are USD and only CHARACTERIZE a separately-entered capital gain; here the FCY concepts ARE the income and count exactly once.
